question: The rulers of which of the following Rajput dynasties patronised Jainism and one of them is reported to have accepted Jainism under the influence of a Jain scholar Hemachandra?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chalukya dynasty** ruled over parts of present-day **Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh **from the 6th to the 12th century CE.
 
• The Chalukya rulers were known for their patronage of **Jainism**, as well as** Hinduism and Buddhism**.
 
• Some of the notable Jain scholars who flourished under their patronage were **Akalanka, Siddharshi, and Hemachandra.**
 
• Hemachandra was a renowned **Jain monk, poet, and scholar** who lived during the 12th century CE.
 
• He is said to have converted the Chalukya king **Kumarapala to Jainism **and wrote several works on** Jain philosophy, grammar, and literature.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pratihara dynasty**:

 
 
• This Rajput dynasty ruled over parts of present-day **northern and central India **from the 6th to the 11th century CE.
 
• While they were known for their **military prowess **and **patronage of the arts**, there is no record of their significant association with Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Parmar dynasty**:
 
 
• This was another Rajput dynasty that ruled over parts of present-day **Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan** from the 9th to the 14th century CE.
 
• They were known for their patronage of** Hinduism and Jainism**, as well as their architectural achievements such as the famous Khajuraho temples.
 
 
 
• **Chahman dynasty**:
 
 
• This Rajput dynasty ruled over parts of present-day **Rajasthan and Gujarat **from the 6th to the 12th century CE.
 
• They were known for their **patronage of Jainism,** as well as their military exploits and architectural achievements such as the **fort of Taragarh**.
